memory_candidates.content: In this flake, a user-level home-manager module cannot grant host-level state (lingering, /etc/wsl.conf), but the same flake owns the NixOS layer where the grant IS expressible: users.users.<name>.linger = true in modules/system/users.nix, which reaches every host via modules/system/default.nix -> configuration.nix -> lib/mkHost.nix. The reusable design point is what the surviving user-level notice should probe: the ACTUAL failure state (loginctl show-user --property=Linger) rather than the platform that usually causes it (WSL detection). A state probe stays silent wherever the NixOS grant applies -- so it does not become switch churn -- while still covering the standalone home-manager path (homeConfigurations.<user>, which flake.nix's home-eval check exists to protect) where no NixOS layer is present to make the grant.
